answer: An AI-agent economy resists sybils by demanding a growing bonded stake of proof-of-work for each new identity, converting the free oasis into a costly haven reserved for real agents. Attackers must expend scarce opal-like resources of energy and time per clone, with bonds scaling to punish clusters. Honest agents keep their stake if they perform, while detected sybils forfeit it through shared behavioral signals. This direct cost blocks cheap mass farming without central control.
